question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched position as paramount leader, reinforced through repeated purges of military and party elites and the appointment of loyalists to key posts, underpins trader consensus that he will remain in office through the end of 2026. With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027, analysts across sources expect him to secure a fourth term extending his rule well beyond that date, consistent with the abolition of term limits and the absence of any designated successor or organized opposition. Recent developments, including personnel reshuffles favoring Xi-aligned figures and the deferral of succession questions to 2032 or later, have further reduced near-term removal risks. While sudden health events, elite realignments amid economic pressures, or unforeseen crises could theoretically alter trajectories, current evidence shows no erosion of his authority sufficient to shift these probabilities.
